sources.title: Single-cell sequencing of immune cells after marathon and symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise
sources.population: Healthy adults; 3 non-regular exercisers assigned to symptom-limited CPX and 3 regular marathon runners; separate short-exercise and marathon groups.
sources.design: Longitudinal PBMC scRNA-seq after one acute bout in two very small groups; not a randomized within-person comparison of CPX versus marathon.
sources.sample_size: 6 participants total (3 CPX, 3 marathon); 12 serial libraries per group reported.
sources.exercise_context: 10–15 min symptom-limited treadmill CPX in the CPX group; approximately 4 h marathon in regular runners.
sources.sampling_times: Pre-exercise, 5 min, 1 h, and 4 h after CPX; pre-exercise, 5 min, 1 h, and 24 h after marathon.
sources.biomarkers: PBMC scRNA-seq, cell-type proportions/subsets, transcript and pathway scores including cytotoxicity, trafficking, and monocyte state.
sources.key_finding: Circulating cell composition shifted over time; T-cell/cytotoxic transcriptional signatures after marathon recovered later than cell abundance. Effector/naive T-cell ratio was proposed as a more uniform acute response indicator than CD4/CD8 ratio.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No prospectively measured infection incidence, viral challenge, or clinical immune-protection outcome; immune function language is based mainly on RNA/pathway or abundance signatures.
sources.validation: scRNA-seq resource deposited at NODE and public; no independent cohort or functional replication reported; no original code reported.
sources.limitations: n=3 per group; habitual training differs by group and is confounded with exercise type/duration; cell-level observations do not replace participant-level replication; functional and infection claims are not established by pathway scores.
sources.evidence_anchor: Abstract; Results: Experimental design; Methods: Participants and exercise protocol; Data and code availability.
sources.integrity_notes: This is the 2023 iScience seed study. Do not report inferred cytotoxicity/antiviral pathway activity as measured killing or infection susceptibility.

sources.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Analysis Reveals Exercise-Induced Transcriptional Dynamics in Half-Marathon Runners
sources.population: Self-reportedly healthy amateur runners, age 29 ± 5 y; 2 men and 2 women were enrolled at a Verona 21.1-km event.
sources.design: Paired PBMC scRNA-seq pre/post half-marathon, followed by cell-type and participant-paired pseudo-bulk analyses.
sources.sample_size: 4 recruited; 3 participants yielded QC-usable libraries; effective paired analysis n=3 participants (6 pre/post participant samples), 4,211 QC-passing cells. One runner’s samples did not yield libraries of sufficient quality. Cells are not independent biological replicates.
sources.exercise_context: 21.1-km half-marathon; event-based acute endurance exercise in amateur runners.
sources.sampling_times: Pre-run 60–90 min before scheduled start; post-run 15–30 min after arrival, approximately 3 h after start. No later recovery sample.
sources.biomarkers: PBMC scRNA-seq in 9 annotated cell types, cell abundance and differential expression/pathway analyses, including platelet signal.
sources.key_finding: Cell-specific myeloid stress/viral-process, lymphoid activation, and platelet/coagulation transcript patterns were reported; classical-monocyte chemokine/IL1B-related transcripts were among decreases. Viral pathway enrichment is a gene-set annotation, not evidence of infection.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No measured infection, immune challenge, or ex vivo functional outcome.
sources.validation: Sequencing data publicly deposited at ENA project PRJEB76303; paired pseudo-bulk DESeq2 at participant sample level; no external cohort.
sources.limitations: Only 3 effective pairs, single immediate post-race time point, observational event setting; high risk of unstable estimates despite thousands of cells; platelets may reflect residual contamination; no functional or clinical endpoint.
sources.evidence_anchor: Full-text Methods 2.1 (enrollment/sampling; PDF p.1), Results (QC exclusion; PDF p.2), Methods 2.5 (paired pseudo-bulk; PDF p.2), and Data Availability Statement.
sources.integrity_notes: Abstract says n=4 collected; Methods state one participant's samples did not yield libraries of adequate quality and were excluded. For inference use effective n=3 paired people, not 4 and not 4,211 cells. Same Verona Run 4 Science context is separate from Yu's Chinese cohorts; no evidence these are the same individuals.

sources.title: Molecular Choreography of Acute Exercise
sources.population: 36 well-characterized adult volunteers, including insulin-sensitive and insulin-resistant participants.
sources.design: Longitudinal controlled symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise test with plasma/PBMC multi-omics and bulk PBMC RNA-seq.
sources.sampling_times: Baseline, then recovery at 2, 15, 30, and 60 min after exercise (the study reports peak transcript changes at 2 min; no exercise-time blood sample).
sources.biomarkers: Bulk PBMC RNA-seq plus immunome, proteome, metabolome, lipidome and clinical CPX phenotyping.
sources.key_finding: Thousands of transcripts responded rapidly; 93.7% of the exercise-responsive transcript set returned to baseline within 60 min. Acute pathways included early immune and oxidative-stress changes. This supports strongly time-dependent/transient expression rather than a universal fixed-duration immune suppression interval.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No post-exercise infection surveillance or immune challenge; fitness prediction analyses are within-cohort and concern VO2/physiology, not infection risk.
sources.validation: Raw/processed multi-omic data were made available through the Stanford Human Microbiome Project portal; extensive within-cohort longitudinal profiling, no independent external clinical validation.
sources.limitations: Bulk PBMC averages can conflate cell-intrinsic expression and exercise-driven cell redistribution; no direct pathogen defense endpoint; fitness model association does not validate immune risk prediction.
sources.evidence_anchor: Abstract; Results: multi-omic changes/time-series PBMC gene expression; Data Availability Statement.
sources.integrity_notes: Independent Stanford cohort from later German and Italian studies; no trial-registration overlap with them identified.

sources.title: Endurance training attenuates acute exercise-induced monocyte transcriptomic responses in adolescents: sex-specific molecular adaptations
sources.population: Healthy adolescents aged 13–17 years: 12 males and 9 females; competitive athletes and chronic conditions were excluded.
sources.design: Within-participant acute exercise challenge before and after an 8-week supervised endurance-training intervention (with brief supplementary strength work).
sources.sample_size: 21 enrolled; 83 RNA-seq samples available from 84 planned timepoint samples (one post-training post-exercise sample missing). Two pre-training samples from one male identified as PCA outliers were excluded from downstream differential-expression analyses (81 sample libraries remain).
sources.exercise_context: Acute challenge was 10 × 2-min cycling bouts at 70% of maximal work rate, separated by 1-min rest; repeated before and after 8 weeks of training (3 sessions/week, 60 min/session).
sources.sampling_times: At each acute challenge, blood was collected at baseline after 30-min catheter equilibration and immediately after exercise; challenges were before training and after the 8-week intervention. No recovery time course.
sources.biomarkers: Isolated circulating monocytes; bulk poly(A)-selected mRNA RNA-seq (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, paired-end 2×100 bp, ~30 million reads/sample), CBC/monocyte counts and lactate. One lncRNA (SCAMP1-AS1) is reported among shared exercise-responsive transcripts; assay is not a comprehensive ncRNA-seq assay.
sources.key_finding: Before training, acute exercise altered 567 transcripts in males and 5,135 in females; after training, 165 and 94 transcripts, respectively (FDR<0.1). The GEO series abstract has slightly different DEG totals (571/5,148), so final article values are used and the metadata discrepancy is flagged.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No infection surveillance, pathogen challenge, or direct monocyte functional assay. CBC/monocyte counts and lactate were measured; pathway results do not establish immune protection or dysfunction.
sources.validation: Raw RNA-seq data are public in GEO GSE324210; no external validation cohort. Linear models with FDR<0.1 were used for paired comparisons; exploratory threshold and within-person design should be retained in interpretation.
sources.limitations: Adolescent single-center cohort, modest n, immediate-only post-exercise sample, one missing sample and two outlier samples excluded. Isolated bulk monocytes reduce whole-blood/PBMC mixture confounding, but monocyte subset immunophenotyping was not performed; exercise mobilization/subset shifts may still contribute. Transcriptomic attenuation after training is not a functional assay.
sources.evidence_anchor: Abstract; Methods: Study Design, Blood Sampling and Analysis, Library Construction, Bioinformatic Analysis; Results; Data Availability; GEO GSE324210.
sources.integrity_notes: Distinct adolescent UCI cohort from Yu/Veschetti/Stanford/MoTrPAC cohorts. Do not equate transcript counts or inferred cardiovascular pathways with direct immune function or clinical infection risk. GEO series abstract and final article report modestly different transcript counts; cite final peer-reviewed article values (567/5,135 pre-training) and preserve this version discrepancy.

sources.title: Transcriptomic analyses of peripheral blood mononuclear cells reveal age-specific basal and acute exercise responsiveness differences in humans
sources.population: Healthy adults free of overt cardiovascular/metabolic disease: young 23 ± 4 y and older 65 ± 7 y.
sources.design: Paired bulk PBMC RNA-seq before and immediately after acute knee-extension exercise, with age-stratified groups.
sources.sample_size: 15 total: young n=7 (2 men, 5 women), older n=8 (4 men, 4 women).
sources.sampling_times: Immediately before and within 1 min of exercise cessation.
sources.biomarkers: PBMC RNA-seq and plasma IL-6/TNF-alpha concentrations.
sources.key_finding: 53 genes changed in the young group and 1,026 in the older group; NK-related enrichment was reported in the young group and immune-signaling differences in older adults. Authors explicitly say cytotoxicity was not measured.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No infection outcome and no direct cytotoxicity, proliferation, or stimulated immune assay.
sources.validation: RNA-seq data public in GEO GSE293163; no independent validation cohort.
sources.limitations: Small age-stratified groups, single immediate post sample, bulk-PBMC cellular composition confounding, exploratory pathway inference, no functional readout.
sources.evidence_anchor: Abstract; Methods: Participants/Experimental Design; Results: Exercise-induced changes; Discussion; Data availability.
sources.integrity_notes: Age is deliberately contrasted with exercise exposure; don't interpret DEG counts as age-specific immune protection or as functional NK cytotoxicity.

sources.title: Maximal and sub-maximal exercise tests alter PBMC microRNA expression: insights into sport- and sex-specific variations
sources.population: 58 healthy participants: 22 runners (9 women), 18 cyclists (9 women), and 18 active controls (9 women); groups differed by habitual sport/training volume.
sources.design: PBMC small-RNA sequencing before/immediately after maximal and submaximal sport-specific tests; sport/sex association analyses.
sources.sample_size: 58 participants (22 runners, 18 cyclists, 18 active controls); repeat exercise tests in the cohort.
sources.exercise_context: VO2max maximal test and a separate time-to-exhaustion test at 85% VO2max, performed one week apart; runners/cyclists exercised in their sport mode.
sources.sampling_times: Pre and immediately post each test; no recovery series.
sources.biomarkers: PBMC small-RNA-seq, PBMC and leukocyte counts, training-volume and exercise-performance covariates.
sources.key_finding: Large group-specific miRNA differences reported (e.g., 279 miRNAs in runners versus 7 in cyclists after maximal test); signal is exploratory and may reflect cell mobilization/composition, training history, mode and sex.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No immune-function assay or prospective infection endpoint. Associations with time-to-exhaustion/training volume are not external prediction validation.
sources.validation: GEO GSE288760 / SRA available; no external cohort. Publisher correction dated 2025-11-07 only corrected an author affiliation.
sources.limitations: Bulk PBMC miRNA cannot distinguish within-cell regulation from cell-subset shifts; tests differ by mode/training history; no recovery/function/infection outcomes; numerical inconsistencies among subgroup significant/upregulated miRNA counts in the article mean those subgroup counts should not be reused without reanalysis.
sources.evidence_anchor: Abstract; Methods: Exercise tests/Blood collection/Statistics; Results; Data Availability; 2025 correction notice.
sources.integrity_notes: A 2025 correction changed affiliation only. Full paper reports subgroup counts that do not reconcile arithmetically (e.g. upregulated count exceeds significant total in a subgroup); treat specific sex-stratified counts as uncertain.

sources.title: Non-coding RNAs in exercise immunology: A systematic review
sources.authors: Mona Kotewitsch, Melina Heimer, Boris Schmitz, Frank C. Mooren
sources.population: Systematic review of exercise interventions in healthy humans; 95 eligible studies entered miRNA synthesis.
sources.design: Systematic review and qualitative evidence grading of human exercise-related ncRNA literature, with immune target databases added for miRNAs.
sources.exercise_context: Acute and chronic exercise, endurance and resistance modalities; review is heterogeneous by protocol and assay.
sources.sampling_times: Study-specific; review separates acute and chronic categories but no single pooled time point.
sources.biomarkers: 164 miRNAs across review-filtered exercise studies; 6 studies covering lncRNAs/circRNAs; 20 lncRNAs and 1 circRNA identified as possible exercise-immunology regulators.
sources.key_finding: 15 endurance-associated miRNAs met the review's consistency threshold, mostly with acute endurance evidence; evidence for lncRNA/circRNA remained sparse.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No pooled clinical infection endpoint; proposed immune actions derive from target/pathway mapping and source studies.
sources.validation: Review searches PubMed, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus and validated-target resources; authors rated overall risk of bias high.
sources.limitations: Heterogeneous designs; database target validation does not demonstrate in vivo mediation by exercise; six lnc/circ studies only; high overall risk of bias.
sources.evidence_anchor: PubMed Abstract; Results/figure caption describing searches, eligible studies and risk of bias.
sources.integrity_notes: Online first 2023-11-03; journal issue is 2024. Do not treat database-predicted target genes as experimental immune function.

sources.title: Acute exercise boosts NAD+ metabolism of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells
sources.population: Healthy young adults in two exercise trials.
sources.design: Two complementary repeated-sampling trials using targeted PBMC gene/protein and NAD metabolite assays; not transcriptome-wide RNA-seq.
sources.sample_size: Trial 1 randomized crossover n=24 (12 women); separate longitudinal kinetics trial n=12 (6 women).
sources.exercise_context: Trial 1 compared time/energy-matched HIIT and moderate continuous exercise; trial 2 used a single cycling bout.
sources.sampling_times: Trial 1 pre, exercise-related serial points, immediate post and 1 h post; trial 2 eight time points from baseline through exercise to 1 h recovery.
sources.biomarkers: Targeted NAD biosynthetic enzyme mRNA and protein abundance, intracellular PBMC NAD+, serum nicotinamide and related metabolites.
sources.key_finding: NAMPT and other NAD-related enzyme transcripts changed acutely; NAMPT response accompanied increases in PBMC NAD+ and protein abundance, providing molecular-to-metabolite concordance.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No infection or direct immune effector-function outcome; metabolite/protein corroboration supports the biochemical mechanism but not a clinical immune benefit.
sources.validation: Separate 12-person kinetics cohort supports temporal replication within the same research program; targeted endpoints, no external group.
sources.limitations: Targeted panel, small young cohorts, blood cell redistribution not eliminated by PBMC bulk measurements, no infection/function readout; trial 1 DRKS00017686 overlaps with other German exercise-immunology reports, so check registration before counting those as independent cohorts.
sources.evidence_anchor: PubMed Abstract; full-text Results and Methods: randomized crossover and longitudinal exercise trials.
sources.integrity_notes: Published online November 2024; journal issue volume is 2025. Trial 1 shares registration DRKS00017686 with a 2025 PBMC proteomics report (not counted here as a separate RNA study).

sources.title: Dynamic transcriptomic responses to divergent acute exercise stimuli in young adults
sources.population: Healthy, previously untrained young adults aged 18–27 y, randomized to combined exercise modalities.
sources.design: Acute randomized TRAD versus HITT protocol; small/long/circular RNA sequencing of skeletal muscle and serum-derived extracellular vesicles.
sources.sample_size: 40 participants total: TRAD n=21 (12 men, 9 women); HITT n=19 (11 men, 8 women).
sources.exercise_context: TRAD combined steady-state cycling and resistance exercise (~90 min); HITT combined maximal intervals and intensive resistance exercise (~45 min); modalities were not duration/work-matched.
sources.sampling_times: Serum EV samples pre, immediately post (h0), 3 h, 24 h; muscle biopsy pre, 3 h, 24 h.
sources.biomarkers: Protein-coding and noncoding RNA, including miRNA, lncRNA and circRNA, in skeletal muscle and serum EVs.
sources.key_finding: EV and muscle RNA profiles changed across time/modalities; some EV pathways were annotated to leukocyte activation/immune response. circRNA findings were sparse; authors note EV cell/tissue origins and lncRNA function need experimental validation.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No immune functional assay, infection outcome, or cell-specific immune assay; immune annotations are indirect EV gene/pathway signatures.
sources.validation: FASTQ/raw counts available at GEO GSE209880; no external cohort or functional validation.
sources.limitations: Muscle and EV fractions are not PBMC/immune-cell transcriptomes; serum EV source and cargo function uncertain; modalities differ in duration and exercise dose; pathway inference does not establish immune activity.
sources.evidence_anchor: Abstract; Methods: exercise/sampling/RNA isolation; Results: EV transcriptomics; Discussion; Data availability.
sources.integrity_notes: Use as adjacent evidence for circulating EV and noncoding RNA discovery, not as direct evidence of leukocyte-intrinsic immunological biomarkers.

sources.title: Blood Biochemical Responses to Acute Exercise: Findings from the Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC)
sources.authors: Jeremy M. Robbins, Daniel H. Katz, Gina M. Many et al.; MoTrPAC Study Group
sources.population: Sedentary, medically screened adults randomized to acute endurance, resistance, or non-exercise control; enrollment stopped during COVID-19 pandemic.
sources.design: Large randomized acute exercise/control multi-omic blood profiling; second version of a bioRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed as of cutoff.
sources.sample_size: 175 participants with at least one blood multi-omic sample; whole-blood transcriptomics n=173; group sizes at baseline acute bout EE=66, RE=73, CON=37 before biospecimen losses.
sources.exercise_context: EE: 40 min cycling around 65% VO2peak; RE: 8 upper/lower-body exercises, 3 sets of 8–12 repetitions to volitional fatigue; non-exercise control.
sources.sampling_times: Up to 7 time points during and through 24 h; exact times vary by randomized temporal profile/tissue.
sources.biomarkers: Whole-blood RNA-seq plus plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling.
sources.key_finding: Preprint reports 7,066 transcript changes (as well as protein/metabolite changes) comparing exercise with non-exercise control and reports exercise-mode/time-dependent blood molecular and immune-related pathway signals.
sources.clinical_endpoint: No prospective infection endpoint and no direct pathogen-challenge/immune effector assay; molecular associations with fitness/phenotypes are not clinical infection prediction.
sources.validation: Data/code and datasets described by MoTrPAC Data Hub/GitHub and consortium data plan; no independent external validation in this report.
sources.limitations: Version 2 posted 2026-03-11; not peer reviewed; pandemic-interrupted early subset rather than full MoTrPAC trial; blood bulk RNA composition and assay/timepoint sample-size variability remain concerns.
sources.evidence_anchor: bioRxiv v2 posted 2026-03-11; Abstract; Results: research design/clinical characteristics; Methods; NLM preprint status.
sources.integrity_notes: Frontier evidence only, not peer-reviewed; version 2 was posted 2026-03-11 (before the 2026-10-02 cutoff). Keep in a separate frontier/preprint appendix, not the formal core set, because review status and cohort completeness remain provisional. It belongs to the same early MoTrPAC human cohort as the 2026 multi-tissue preprint (DOI 10.64898/2026.02.27.702183); do not double count the two reports as independent cohorts.

findings.claim: 健康人急性运动RNA信号有较强时间依赖性，简单按“运动后30分钟”截断会漏掉运动中、1小时、3–4小时及24小时的差异；一项36人PBMC多组学研究报告大多数转录变化在60分钟内回到基线，马拉松/单细胞研究则显示某些转录或细胞组成信号更久。
findings.certainty: moderate for transient/time-varying expression; low for any universal recovery threshold
findings.protocol_implication: 将采样窗口按运动中/即刻、0–1 h、3–4 h、约24 h分层，记录连续时间；不设统一30分钟规则或由RNA推定感染风险窗口。

findings.claim: scRNA-seq的主要增量是分开细胞组成与细胞内表达，但当前最贴题的人体运动研究有效生物学样本很小：Yu每组3人，Veschetti半马只剩3个有效配对。细胞数不等于受试者数。
findings.protocol_implication: 提取participants n、paired biological samples n、cells n三种分母；标明单细胞pseudo-bulk是否以受试者为统计单位；把小样本研究作为机制/候选证据而非预测验证。

findings.claim: PBMC miRNA、目标mRNA和EV RNA有候选信号，但结果受运动类型、训练背景、性别、采样分数及血液细胞动员影响；ncRNA系统综述发现lncRNA/circRNA人体免疫证据极少且总体偏倚风险高。
findings.certainty: low to moderate for association; low for causal immune function
findings.protocol_implication: 单独归类PBMC miRNA、靶向mRNA、血清EV RNA、肌肉RNA；抽取RNA分馏/平台/细胞计数/批次和验证；不把预测靶点或富集通路升级成体内功能。

findings.claim: 已检索RNA组学研究基本测量表达、通路或细胞比例，未验证运动后临床感染发生率；病毒/抗菌通路富集不能等同病原体感染、功能下降或临床免疫抑制。
findings.protocol_implication: 协议的结果层级应明确区分表达变化、细胞数量/比例、直接免疫功能、感染发生、预后/个体预测；RNA差异只支持候选标志物。

findings.claim: 同一队列重复分析需要审查注册号/时间地点：Walzik的DRKS00017686第一试验与德国2025 PBMC蛋白组研究登记号相同；半马Veschetti、Yu、Stanford 2020、UCI青少年2026及MoTrPAC均为不同队列/项目；MoTrPAC两个2026预印本来自同一早期队列。
findings.certainty: high for registration or source-record overlap where specified; moderate otherwise
findings.protocol_implication: 筛选/提取时以受试者队列、注册号、地点、采样年份建立study-family ID，衍生组学论文合并成同一队列而非独立证据。

gaps: 健康人急性运动转录组与临床感染结局的直接连接缺失；本轮10项来源没有一项用前瞻性监测证实感染因果或个体风险预测。
有高时间分辨率但样本小，或样本相对较大但PBMC/全血bulk混杂；需要配套CBC/分类计数、流式或细胞去卷积并以受试者为生物学重复。
健康人体lncRNA/circRNA免疫研究非常稀少；EV来源、RNA cargo功能和靶细胞仍未解决。
研究集中在年轻男性/运动员、少量极端赛事或单中心样本；性别、年龄、月经周期、训练水平、运动模式/剂量间缺少独立验证。
多数数据可公开复用（GEO/ENA/NODE）；部分GEO系列摘要与最终期刊文章的差异表达计数存在轻微版本不一致，应以最终出版稿为准并保留审计记录。
proposed_updates: 新增“转录组与非编码RNA” biomarker family，区分：PBMC/免疫细胞bulk mRNA、whole-blood mRNA、scRNA/pseudo-bulk、PBMC miRNA、血清/EV miRNA及lncRNA/circRNA；肌肉RNA可列为生理机制背景，不与外周免疫细胞混合。
在protocol明确acute bout与training intervention不同层；另编码exercise type/intensity/duration/fitness/training background/sex/age，时间按运动中、即刻、0–1 h、3–4 h、24 h及更晚，不预设30-min门槛。
数据提取时必须分别记受试者总n、有效配对n、RNA样本n、单细胞数；对scRNA记录样本级pseudo-bulk/混合模型和细胞比例分析，单细胞数量不可当独立n。
为whole blood/PBMC标注是否同步CBC/分类计数/流式或去卷积；将细胞比例变化与细胞内表达变化分开，EV RNA/细胞游离RNA不能归因给免疫细胞除非来源被验证。
对每项RNA证据按递进层级提取：表达/细胞比例变化→直接功能测量→感染监测→外部预测验证；GO“viral response”、靶点数据库或组内性能相关不算感染结局/临床预测。
新增版本/队列审查字段：注册号、study family、发布版本、Correction、数据仓库 accession；同注册试验的多组学论文只计一个队列。将GEO摘要与最终出版文中差异表达统计不一致的情况记入版本核查日志。
将MoTrPAC 2026 blood v2作为前沿附录/待同行评审更新项，并于正式五库检索后用受试者数、组别、时间分层及结果完整度复核；不与其同一队列的多组织预印本重复计数。

正式重启使用用户已确认可用的PubMed、Web of Science、Scopus、Embase和SPORTDiscus，按各库语法运行“acute exercise/exercise training × human × blood/PBMC/monocyte × RNA-seq/scRNA-seq/miRNA/lncRNA/circRNA”检索块；由第二位筛选者独立复筛标题摘要和全文，去重后按study-family合并队列。当前lane仅为公共网页定向核验，不能替代数据库导出或形成PRISMA筛选数。
search_limitations: 本轮为定向公共网页/期刊/PubMed/PMC/NCBI GEO/ENA核查，不是五个订阅数据库的正式检索或系统筛查，不能声称PRISMA流程或穷尽。仅可打开/明确核验的文献入表。部分全文站点对自动访问有验证码或403，已用出版社全文、开放仓储、PubMed/PMC索引和GEO/ENA元数据交叉核对。当前定向范围未检索到临床感染或外部预测验证；该结论仅对本轮纳入来源成立。
